title: Annual modulation as the decisive test for inelastic dark matter near the kinematic edge
question: For inelastic O1 DM at delta = 300/330/350/366/380 keV (1 TeV), what exposure establishes the time dependence of a high-energy NR population at 3/5 sigma against (a) a time-flat signal of equal rate and (b) background only, using a cosine-amplitude estimator, the unbinned time likelihood ratio and summer-window counting, and how do halo tail, efficiency roll-off and livetime gaps change it?
headline_result: Against a time-flat population, 3 sigma needs 5.3/6.5/11.5/29/97 events = 15/19/33/84/274 t yr (5 sigma 40-762 t yr) for delta = 380/366/350/330/300 keV at the best-fit rate; LZ (2.79 t yr/yr) reaches 3 sigma only for delta >= 366 keV around 2029-2030 (median 0.7-2.8 sigma at 12.9 t yr); against the modelled background the rate alone discovers at 10.6 t yr (panel) or 5.0 t yr (neighbourhood) and timing gains <= x1.36; a known-phase cosine test is within 3% of the full likelihood ratio; an ROI extended to 400 keV would reach 3 sigma x2.8 (366) to x21 (380 keV) sooner
model_or_mechanism: WimPyDD O1 isoscalar inelastic per-stream kernels x Baxter-2021 Earth-frame halo on 36 days (periodic spline), Fig. S2 efficiency; exact N-fold FFT convolution of per-event statistics (cosine, log-likelihood ratio with absorbing zero-rate season) for median significance, 1e4-toy cross-check; binomial window test; extended rate+time likelihood vs Poisson counting for discovery; halo (v_esc, v0), efficiency-edge and livetime-gap variants
confidence: high for time-PDF shapes and exact statistics (kernel = wd_rate to 1e-5, toys agree, P018/P020 reproduced); medium for calendar years (rate band, unknown livetime, 60 t assumptions)
agent_tools: Read x17, Bash x15, Write x5, Edit x11, Skill x1 (dataviz)
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (diff_rate sum_over_streams=False, streamed_halo_function explicit vmin, eft_hamiltonian); numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (fft, CubicSpline, stats); pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
